turns.t: Mr Okonkwo, is it? I've got your discharge letter from the hospital here, and I've updated your phone number. ~
That's right, though I've told you lot three times, I'm Christopher, not Chris, but never mind. Oh, and the hospital lost my glasses, did they tell you? ~
I'm Nurse Ruth, Mr Okonkwo. I'll bring you through. The doctor's got your letter. ~
Take a seat, Christopher. I'm Dr Banerjee. You were in for pneumonia, I see. How are you feeling now?
Better, much better, thank you. The food in there, though, honestly, a week of chicken that tasted of nothing. ~
Hospital food, yes. Any cough left?
A little, yes, in the morning. A dry one. It's much better than it was.
And your energy?
Tired, I still get tired by three o'clock. I was at the gym four times a week and now I can barely make the shops.
Understandable, that takes weeks. Any fever since you came home?
No, no temperature, I've been checking.
Any breathlessness, even on the stairs?
Not really. A bit on the hill, but not on the stairs.
Any chest pain?
No, none whatsoever.
Are you still on antibiotics?
Yes, the last few days. Clarithromycin, maybe 500 mg? Twice a day. Honestly I'd have to look at the box, my daughter sorts them out.
Your letter says the course ends on Friday, Mr Okonkwo.
Good, finish it. And do you smoke?
I gave it up when I went into hospital. Twenty a day, for thirty years, and I haven't touched one since.
That's a big change, well done. How are you managing the cravings? ~
Terrible, honestly, but my daughter hid my lighter. ~
Keep that up. Smoking is the main thing that will help your lungs now. ~
I know. She says that every day. ~
Doctor, shall I book his follow-up appointment? ~
Yes please, Joy. Christopher, I'd like to arrange a repeat chest X-ray in six weeks, to be sure the pneumonia has cleared completely.
Six weeks. Is that normal, to repeat it? ~
Yes, in people over fifty who smoked, we always check, to make sure nothing else is hiding behind the infection. ~
I see. Right. ~
Keep drinking plenty, build up walking gradually, and rest when you need to.
I'll try, though the stairs at home are a trial. ~
And I'd like to see you again in six weeks with the X-ray.
I'll put it in for you, Mr Okonkwo, after you've seen the nurse. ~
Thank you all. And if you find my glasses, tell the hospital they're brown. ~

negative_findings.normalized_name: Breathlessness at rest or on stairs

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient gave the clarithromycin dose tentatively ("maybe 500 mg") and would need to check the box.
